group: The Supernatural: The Devil, Demons & Angels
belief: Satan has power over me, and I am helpless.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that Satan has power over you and you are helpless, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Frightening stories or movies about demonic power. Teaching that focused more on the devil’s strength than on Christ’s victory. Long struggles with temptation, fear, or dark thoughts that seem impossible to escape. Past involvement in the occult. Trauma that left you feeling powerless in general.
teaches: Satan is real, but he is a defeated enemy. At the cross, Christ disarmed the powers and authorities and triumphed over them. The One who lives in you is greater than the one who is in the world. You are not helpless: you can submit to God, resist the devil, and he will flee. The Lord is faithful to strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.
self_statements: The devil is stronger than I am.
Evil has a hold on me I can’t break.
I’m just a victim of spiritual forces.
errors: Making the enemy look bigger than Christ.
Believing you have no choices or power when God has given you both.
Concluding “I feel powerless, so I am powerless.”
Focusing on the devil’s schemes while ignoring Christ’s victory.
Predicting you will always be defeated.
questions: Who is greater: the One in me or the one in the world?
What happened to the powers and authorities at the cross?
What does James 4:7 say will happen when I resist the devil?
Is it possible I have given the devil more credit than Scripture does?
What choices do I still have, even in this struggle?
Has God ever helped me resist something before?
Who promises to guard me from the evil one?
truth: Satan does not have the final power over me. Jesus defeated him at the cross, and the One who lives in me is greater. I am not helpless: I can submit to God and resist the devil, and he will flee. The Lord is faithful to strengthen me and guard me. In Christ I am more than a conqueror.
hw_questions: Who is greater: the One in me or the one in the world?
What happened to evil powers at the cross?
What does James 4:7 promise when I resist?
Have I given the devil more credit than Scripture does?
What choices do I still have?
hw_truths: Greater is He who is in me than he who is in the world.
Jesus defeated Satan at the cross.
When I resist the devil, he will flee.
The Lord is faithful to guard me from the evil one.
In Christ I am more than a conqueror.
I am not helpless; I have choices and God’s strength.
log: Each day, write one way I resisted a lie or temptation, however small, and thank God for His strength.
name_example: But the Lord is faithful, and He will strengthen Sarah and guard her from the evil one.
actions: When the fear or temptation comes,
say aloud, “Greater is He who is in me,” then take one small step of obedience.
Remove one thing from your home or phone
and write how each piece of armor applies to your struggle.
Ask a pastor or trusted believer to pray with you,
and notice how it feels to not fight alone.
prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You that You triumphed over every evil power at the cross. Help me reject the lie that Satan has power over me and that I am helpless. I submit myself to You. Strengthen me, guard me from the evil one, and help me stand firm. You are greater than anything I face. In Your name, Amen.
